summary: CWE-111 Direct Use of Unsafe JNI: the bad() method reads an attacker-controlled string and an independently-parsed integer length from the console and passes both straight to the native method test(String, int). Because the native C code trusts the Java-supplied length to index/copy the string, a length that exceeds the actual string size causes an out-of-bounds read/write in native code. The fix validates the untrusted length against the actual string before crossing the JNI boundary (and guards against a null line), clamping an out-of-range length to the real string length. Valid inputs where the length matches the string still work unchanged, and the native call is preserved.
